programme.displayName: Amazon EC2: Secure, Resilient, and Auto Scaled Web Infrastructure
programme.subtitle: Build, operate, protect, load balance, scale, monitor, and safely remove a complete EC2 web environment.
programme.description: Start with no learner infrastructure and complete six connected EC2 labs in eu-west-2. Create dedicated access and networking, launch and manage Amazon Linux through Session Manager, protect EBS data, build a two-AZ Application Load Balancer design, add Auto Scaling and CloudWatch, audit operations, compare SAA-C03 architecture choices, and remove every training resource.
programme.learningOutcome: Build and explain secure EC2 infrastructure using both the AWS Console and CLI; operate instances without SSH; recover EBS data; create a highly available load-balanced web tier; configure self-healing and target tracking; monitor and audit operations; choose suitable purchasing and placement strategies; and perform complete reverse-order cleanup.

tasks.title: Create the dedicated training IAM user and verify its CLI identity
tasks.feature: IAM user, console sign-in, and programmatic CLI access
tasks.goal: Create fa-ec2-learner, give it a policy limited to the named EC2 lab resources and the fixed SSM instance role/profile, create console and CLI credentials, and verify the CLI identity.
tasks.whyItMatters: The administrator performs initial identity setup. The learner then uses a separate IAM user with only the permissions required to create, operate, inspect, and remove this lab's VPC, EC2, EBS, and Systems Manager resources.

consoleSteps.title: Create the learner user and restricted policy as an administrator
consoleSteps.instruction: Sign in to the AWS Management Console using an administrator-capable identity. Do not perform this setup while signed in as the future learner user.

instructions.text: Sign in to the AWS Management Console using an administrator-capable identity. Do not perform this setup while signed in as the future learner user.
In the top navigation search box, enter IAM, then choose IAM.
In the left navigation pane, choose Users, then choose Create user.
For User name, enter fa-ec2-learner.
Select Provide user access to the AWS Management Console.
Select I want to create an IAM user.
Select Custom password, enter a unique password, and select Users must create a new password at next sign-in.
Choose Next, select Attach policies directly, then choose Create policy.
Choose the JSON tab, replace all editor content with the supplied policy JSON, then choose Next.
For Policy name, enter fa-ec2-learner-lab-policy. Choose Create policy.
Return to the Create user browser tab. Choose the refresh control beside the policy list, select fa-ec2-learner-lab-policy, choose Next, then choose Create user.
Choose the fa-ec2-learner user name. Record the Console sign-in URL shown on the user page as [IAM_SIGN_IN_URL]. This is the account-specific URL used in the next step.
Choose Security credentials. Under Access keys, choose Create access key.
Select Command Line Interface (CLI), select the confirmation checkbox, choose Next, then choose Create access key.

Download the CSV or store the access key ID and secret access key in a secure password manager. The access key ID identifies the credential; the secret access key is shown only once and authenticates CLI requests.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: fa-ec2-learner exists, has fa-ec2-learner-lab-policy attached, has console access, and has one new CLI access key.
consoleSteps.warning: Never share the password, secret access key, downloaded CSV, or CloudShell credential files. The policy deliberately permits only the named lab role/profile to be passed to EC2.

consoleSteps.title: Sign in as the learner and create the CLI profile
consoleSteps.instruction: Open a private browser window and browse to [IAM_SIGN_IN_URL]. [IAM_SIGN_IN_URL] is the account-specific IAM user sign-in URL recorded in the previous step.

instructions.text: Open a private browser window and browse to [IAM_SIGN_IN_URL]. [IAM_SIGN_IN_URL] is the account-specific IAM user sign-in URL recorded in the previous step.
Enter fa-ec2-learner for IAM user name and enter the password created for this user.
Complete the required password change.
Open CloudShell from the console navigation bar.
At the CloudShell prompt, run the aws configure command in the CLI route below.
When prompted, enter the fa-ec2-learner access key ID and secret access key created in the preceding step. Enter eu-west-2 for Default region name and json for Default output format.
Run the get-caller-identity command in the CLI route below. Record Account as [ACCOUNT_ID] only if you need to identify the account later.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The identity response contains an ARN ending in user/fa-ec2-learner.
consoleSteps.warning: aws configure stores credentials in the CloudShell home directory. Remove the profile after cleanup if the CloudShell environment will continue to be used.

cliSteps.command: aws iam create-user --user-name fa-ec2-learner
cliSteps.explanation: Run as the original administrator to create the learner identity.
cliSteps.warning: IAM is global; do not specify a Region.

cliSteps.command: aws configure --profile fa-ec2-learner
cliSteps.explanation: Run after securely obtaining the learner access key. Supply credentials only at prompts, use eu-west-2 as the default Region, and use json as the default output format.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The profile is written after all prompts complete.
cliSteps.warning: Do not place credential values on the command line.

cliSteps.command: aws sts get-caller-identity --profile fa-ec2-learner
cliSteps.explanation: Confirm that subsequent CLI commands use the dedicated learner identity.
cliSteps.warning: Do not continue with the learner CLI route if the ARN identifies the administrator instead.

verification.title: Verify the active learner identity
verification.instruction: Run aws sts get-caller-identity --profile fa-ec2-learner in CloudShell or a local terminal.
verification.expectedResult: The returned ARN ends in user/fa-ec2-learner rather than identifying the administrator.

tasks.title: Create the VPC, public subnet, gateway, route table, and web security group
tasks.goal: Build an isolated 10.0.0.0/16 VPC with one public 10.0.1.0/24 subnet and a security group that permits browser HTTP traffic only from the learner's current public IPv4 address.
tasks.whyItMatters: For SAA-C03, a subnet becomes public because its associated route table has a route to an internet gateway; assigning a public IPv4 address alone is not enough. Security groups are stateful virtual firewalls attached to the instance network interface.

consoleSteps.title: Create the VPC and public subnet
consoleSteps.instruction: ☐ In the AWS Console search box, enter VPC.

instructions.text: ☐ In the AWS Console search box, enter VPC.
☐ Choose VPC.
☐ Confirm Region is Europe (London) eu-west-2.
☐ In the left navigation pane, choose Your VPCs.
☐ Choose Create VPC.
☐ Select VPC only.
☐ Enter fa-ec2-vpc in Name tag - optional.
☐ Enter 10.0.0.0/16 in IPv4 CIDR block.
☐ Leave IPv6 CIDR block set to No IPv6 CIDR block.
☐ Leave Tenancy set to Default.
☐ Choose Create VPC.
☐ In the left navigation pane, choose Subnets.
☐ Choose Create subnet.
☐ Select fa-ec2-vpc in VPC ID.
☐ Enter fa-ec2-public-subnet in Subnet name.
☐ Select eu-west-2a in Availability Zone.
☐ Enter 10.0.1.0/24 in IPv4 VPC CIDR block.
☐ Choose Create subnet.
☐ Select fa-ec2-public-subnet.
☐ Choose Actions.
☐ Choose Edit subnet settings.
☐ Select Enable auto-assign public IPv4 address.
☐ Choose Save.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The VPC has CIDR 10.0.0.0/16. The subnet has CIDR 10.0.1.0/24 in eu-west-2a and automatically assigns public IPv4 addresses to launched instances.
consoleSteps.warning: Availability Zone names can be mapped differently between AWS accounts. If eu-west-2a is unavailable in the selector, use the first available eu-west-2 Availability Zone and record it as [LAB_AZ].

consoleSteps.title: Create public routing and the security group
consoleSteps.instruction: ☐ In the VPC left navigation pane, choose Internet gateways.

instructions.text: ☐ In the VPC left navigation pane, choose Internet gateways.
☐ Choose Create internet gateway.
☐ Enter fa-ec2-igw in Name tag.
☐ Choose Create internet gateway.
☐ Choose Actions.
☐ Choose Attach to VPC.
☐ Select fa-ec2-vpc.
☐ Choose Attach internet gateway.
☐ In the left navigation pane, choose Route tables.
☐ Choose Create route table.
☐ Enter fa-ec2-public-rt in Name tag.
☐ Select fa-ec2-vpc in VPC.
☐ Choose Create route table.
☐ Select fa-ec2-public-rt.
☐ Choose the Routes tab.
☐ Choose Edit routes.
☐ Choose Add route.
☐ Enter 0.0.0.0/0 in Destination.
☐ Select Internet Gateway in Target.
☐ Select fa-ec2-igw in Internet Gateway.
☐ Choose Save changes.
☐ Choose the Subnet associations tab.
☐ Choose Edit subnet associations.
☐ Select fa-ec2-public-subnet.
☐ Choose Save associations.
☐ In the VPC left navigation pane, choose Security groups.
☐ Choose Create security group.
☐ Enter fa-ec2-web-sg in Security group name.
☐ Enter HTTP access for the fa-ec2 training website in Description.
☐ Select fa-ec2-vpc in VPC.
☐ Under Inbound rules, choose Add rule.
☐ Select HTTP in Type.
☐ Select My IP in Source.
☐ Choose Create security group.
☐ Record the Security group ID value on the security group details page as [WEB_SG_ID].

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The selected route table has a 0.0.0.0/0 route whose target is fa-ec2-igw and is associated with fa-ec2-public-subnet. fa-ec2-web-sg permits TCP port 80 only from the IP address detected by the console.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not add SSH port 22. Session Manager will provide administrative access without an inbound management port.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 create-vpc --cidr-block 10.0.0.0/16 --tag-specifications 'ResourceType=vpc,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-ec2-vpc}]' --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-ec2-learner
cliSteps.explanation: Create the isolated lab VPC. Record VpcId from the response as [VPC_ID].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response contains a Vpc object and its VpcId.
cliSteps.warning: Use [VPC_ID] only after recording it from this response.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 create-subnet --vpc-id [VPC_ID] --cidr-block 10.0.1.0/24 --availability-zone eu-west-2a --tag-specifications 'ResourceType=subnet,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-ec2-public-subnet}]' --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-ec2-learner
cliSteps.explanation: Create the one public-subnet candidate. Record SubnetId as [SUBNET_ID].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response contains SubnetId and AvailabilityZone eu-west-2a.
cliSteps.warning: Replace [VPC_ID] with the recorded VPC ID.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 modify-subnet-attribute --subnet-id [SUBNET_ID] --map-public-ip-on-launch --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-ec2-learner
cliSteps.explanation: Make instances launched in this subnet receive a public IPv4 address, subject to public routing.
cliSteps.warning: This does not itself create internet connectivity; the route table still needs the gateway route.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 create-internet-gateway --tag-specifications 'ResourceType=internet-gateway,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-ec2-igw}]' --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-ec2-learner
cliSteps.explanation: Create the VPC internet gateway. Record InternetGatewayId as [IGW_ID].
cliSteps.warning: The gateway is not usable by the VPC until attached.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 attach-internet-gateway --internet-gateway-id [IGW_ID] --vpc-id [VPC_ID] --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-ec2-learner
cliSteps.explanation: Attach the named lab gateway to the lab VPC.
cliSteps.warning: Replace both placeholders using earlier responses.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 create-route-table --vpc-id [VPC_ID] --tag-specifications 'ResourceType=route-table,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-ec2-public-rt}]' --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-ec2-learner
cliSteps.explanation: Create a separate route table for the public subnet. Record RouteTableId as [RTB_ID].
cliSteps.warning: Do not use the VPC main route table for this training example.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 create-route --route-table-id [RTB_ID] --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --gateway-id [IGW_ID] --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-ec2-learner
cliSteps.explanation: Add the default IPv4 route to the attached internet gateway.
cliSteps.warning: This route makes the associated subnet public.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 associate-route-table --route-table-id [RTB_ID] --subnet-id [SUBNET_ID] --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-ec2-learner
cliSteps.explanation: Associate the public route table with the lab subnet.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response contains an AssociationId; record it as [RTB_ASSOCIATION_ID].
cliSteps.warning: Do not disassociate the VPC main route-table association.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 create-security-group --group-name fa-ec2-web-sg --description 'HTTP access for the fa-ec2 training website' --vpc-id [VPC_ID] --tag-specifications 'ResourceType=security-group,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-ec2-web-sg}]' --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-ec2-learner
cliSteps.explanation: Create the security group attached to the lab VPC. Record GroupId as [WEB_SG_ID].
cliSteps.warning: A new security group has no inbound rules until the next command.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id [WEB_SG_ID] --ip-permissions 'IpProtocol=tcp,FromPort=80,ToPort=80,IpRanges=[{CidrIp=[YOUR_PUBLIC_IPV4_CIDR],Description="Learner browser HTTP"}]' --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-ec2-learner
cliSteps.explanation: Allow only browser HTTP from your current public IPv4 address. Replace [YOUR_PUBLIC_IPV4_CIDR] with the address displayed by the console My IP selector followed by /32, for example 198.51.100.10/32.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response reports the added inbound permission.
cliSteps.warning: Do not use 0.0.0.0/0 for this learner web-server test.

verification.title: Verify public-network ingredients
verification.instruction: In the VPC console, open fa-ec2-public-rt and inspect its Routes and Subnet associations tabs; then open fa-ec2-web-sg and inspect Inbound rules.
verification.expectedResult: The route table associates fa-ec2-public-subnet and routes 0.0.0.0/0 to fa-ec2-igw. The security group has only the HTTP port 80 rule from your /32 source.

tasks.title: Create the Session Manager role and launch Amazon Linux 2023
tasks.feature: IAM instance profile and Amazon EC2
tasks.goal: Create the fixed EC2 Systems Manager role and instance profile, wait until the profile is available, then launch one Amazon Linux 2023 t3.micro instance in the dedicated public subnet.
tasks.whyItMatters: The instance profile supplies the SSM Agent with instance credentials. This separates the EC2 workload role from the IAM user that operates the lab and avoids SSH keys and inbound SSH access.

consoleSteps.title: Create the EC2 Systems Manager role
consoleSteps.instruction: In the AWS Console search box, enter IAM and choose IAM.

instructions.text: In the AWS Console search box, enter IAM and choose IAM.
Choose Roles in the left navigation pane, then choose Create role.
Select AWS service for Trusted entity type. Under Use case, select EC2, then choose Next.
Select AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore, then choose Next.
For Role name, enter fa-ec2-ssm-role. For Description, enter Session Manager role for the fa-ec2 lab.
Choose Create role. The EC2 console creates the matching instance profile for this role.
Wait briefly before launching the instance so the new role and profile are available to EC2.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: fa-ec2-ssm-role has trusted entity ec2.amazonaws.com and AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore attached.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not attach AdministratorAccess to the EC2 role.

consoleSteps.title: Launch the Amazon Linux instance
consoleSteps.instruction: In the AWS Console search box, enter EC2 and choose EC2.

instructions.text: In the AWS Console search box, enter EC2 and choose EC2.
Choose Instances, then choose Launch instances.
For Name and tags, enter fa-ec2-web-01.
Under Application and OS Images, choose Amazon Linux and select the visible Amazon Linux 2023 AMI.
Set Instance type to t3.micro.
For Key pair (login), select Proceed without a key pair (Not recommended).
Under Network settings, choose Edit. Select fa-ec2-vpc for VPC, fa-ec2-public-subnet for Subnet, and Enable for Auto-assign public IP.
Select Select existing security group and select fa-ec2-web-sg.
Open Advanced details and select fa-ec2-ssm-role for IAM instance profile.
Under Configure storage, retain one 8 GiB gp3 root volume. Under Summary, set Number of instances to 1.
Choose Launch instance. Open the i- instance ID link in the success message.
In Details, record Instance ID as [INSTANCE_ID], Public IPv4 address as [PUBLIC_IPV4], Private IPv4 addresses as [PRIVATE_IPV4], and Availability Zone as [INSTANCE_AZ].

consoleSteps.expectedResult: fa-ec2-web-01 reaches Running state with the selected VPC, subnet, security group, SSM role, public and private IPv4 addresses, and one 8 GiB gp3 root volume.
consoleSteps.warning: The automatically assigned public IPv4 address is not durable and can change after a stop/start.

cliSteps.command: aws iam create-role --role-name fa-ec2-ssm-role --assume-role-policy-document '{"Version":"2012-10-17","Statement":[{"Effect":"Allow","Principal":{"Service":"ec2.amazonaws.com"},"Action":"sts:AssumeRole"}]}' --profile fa-ec2-learner
cliSteps.explanation: Create the role trusted by EC2.
cliSteps.warning: IAM is global.

cliSteps.command: aws iam attach-role-policy --role-name fa-ec2-ssm-role --policy-arn arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore --profile fa-ec2-learner
cliSteps.explanation: Attach the AWS-managed policy needed by the SSM Agent.
cliSteps.warning: Attach this policy to the EC2 role, not the learner user.

cliSteps.command: aws iam create-instance-profile --instance-profile-name fa-ec2-ssm-profile --profile fa-ec2-learner
cliSteps.explanation: Create the profile container that EC2 attaches to an instance.
cliSteps.warning: IAM is global.

cliSteps.command: aws iam add-role-to-instance-profile --instance-profile-name fa-ec2-ssm-profile --role-name fa-ec2-ssm-role --profile fa-ec2-learner
cliSteps.explanation: Add the EC2 role to the instance profile.
cliSteps.warning: Wait briefly before the next command because IAM changes can take time to propagate.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 run-instances --image-id resolve:ssm:/aws/service/ami-amazon-linux-latest/al2023-ami-kernel-default-x86_64 --instance-type t3.micro --subnet-id [SUBNET_ID] --security-group-ids [WEB_SG_ID] --iam-instance-profile Name=fa-ec2-ssm-profile --block-device-mappings 'DeviceName=/dev/xvda,Ebs={VolumeSize=8,VolumeType=gp3,DeleteOnTermination=true}' --tag-specifications 'ResourceType=instance,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-ec2-web-01}]' --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-ec2-learner
cliSteps.explanation: Launch the lab instance. [SUBNET_ID] and [WEB_SG_ID] came from Task 2. Record Instances[0].InstanceId as [INSTANCE_ID].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response contains the new instance ID in pending state.
cliSteps.warning: If EC2 reports that the instance profile cannot be found, wait briefly and repeat this same launch command; do not create another role or profile.

verification.title: Verify Systems Manager readiness
verification.instruction: In Systems Manager, choose Fleet Manager, then Managed nodes. Wait for fa-ec2-web-01 to appear.
verification.expectedResult: fa-ec2-web-01 is listed as a managed node, ready for Session Manager without an SSH rule.

tasks.title: Connect with Session Manager and publish Apache
tasks.feature: AWS Systems Manager Session Manager and Apache HTTP Server
tasks.goal: Use Session Manager to install Apache, start it, publish one test page, verify it locally, and then reach it through the instance public IPv4 address.
tasks.whyItMatters: Session Manager provides management access without an inbound SSH rule. The narrowly scoped HTTP rule allows the learner browser to reach Apache while security-group statefulness permits the return traffic.

consoleSteps.title: Connect with Session Manager and configure Apache
consoleSteps.instruction: In the AWS Console search box, enter Systems Manager and choose Systems Manager.

instructions.text: In the AWS Console search box, enter Systems Manager and choose Systems Manager.
In the left navigation pane, choose Session Manager, then choose Start session.
Select fa-ec2-web-01 and choose Start session.
In the session terminal, enter sudo dnf install -y httpd.
After installation completes, enter sudo systemctl enable --now httpd.

Enter echo '

fa-ec2-web-01 is running

' | sudo tee /var/www/html/index.html.
Enter curl http://localhost.
After the heading appears, choose Terminate in the Session Manager toolbar.

consoleSteps.expectedResult:
curl returns

fa-ec2-web-01 is running

, proving Apache is running locally and serving the created page.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not install or configure SSH for this lab.

consoleSteps.title: Open the browser test page
consoleSteps.instruction: In the AWS Console search box, enter EC2 and choose EC2.

instructions.text: In the AWS Console search box, enter EC2 and choose EC2.
Choose Instances, select fa-ec2-web-01, and open the Details tab.
Copy the current Public IPv4 address. This value is [PUBLIC_IPV4].
Open a new browser tab and browse to http://[PUBLIC_IPV4].

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The browser displays fa-ec2-web-01 is running.
consoleSteps.warning: Use http rather than https because this lab configures Apache on port 80 only and does not configure TLS.

cliSteps.command: aws ssm start-session --target [INSTANCE_ID] --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-ec2-learner

tasks.title: Inspect EC2 lifecycle and create the first EBS snapshot
tasks.feature: EC2 instance state, addressing, EBS volume, snapshot, and dependency-safe cleanup
tasks.goal: Inspect instance and storage metadata, observe stop/start behaviour, and create a recoverable EBS snapshot without beginning final cleanup.
tasks.whyItMatters: An EBS-backed instance preserves its root volume and private IPv4 address across stop/start. Its automatically assigned public IPv4 address is released when stopped and can change at restart. Manual EBS snapshots survive deletion of the source volume and must be removed separately.

consoleSteps.title: Inspect the running instance and root volume
consoleSteps.instruction: In the EC2 console, choose Instances and select fa-ec2-web-01.

instructions.text: In the EC2 console, choose Instances and select fa-ec2-web-01.
Open Details. Record the current Public IPv4 address as [PUBLIC_IPV4_BEFORE_STOP], Private IPv4 addresses as [PRIVATE_IPV4], and Instance ID as [INSTANCE_ID].
Open the Security tab and select the fa-ec2-web-sg link. Inspect Inbound rules, then return to the instance.
Open the Storage tab. Record the root Volume ID as [VOLUME_ID], then open its Volume ID link.
Inspect Size, Volume type, State, and Attached instances.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The running instance has fa-ec2-web-sg, and the attached root volume is 8 GiB gp3 in-use.
consoleSteps.warning: The private IPv4 address is for VPC communication, not direct public-internet access.

consoleSteps.title: Stop, restart, and compare addresses
consoleSteps.instruction: Return to EC2 Instances and select fa-ec2-web-01.

instructions.text: Return to EC2 Instances and select fa-ec2-web-01.
Choose Instance state, choose Stop instance, then choose Stop in the confirmation dialog.
Wait until Instance state displays Stopped. Do not expect a Public IPv4 address while stopped; the automatically assigned address was released.
Choose Instance state, choose Start instance, and wait until Instance state displays Running.
In Details, record the current Public IPv4 address as [PUBLIC_IPV4_AFTER_START]. Compare it with [PUBLIC_IPV4_BEFORE_STOP].
Browse to http://[PUBLIC_IPV4_AFTER_START].

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The website works after restart. The root EBS volume and private IPv4 address remain associated; the public IPv4 address may differ from [PUBLIC_IPV4_BEFORE_STOP].
consoleSteps.warning: Stopped instances do not incur instance runtime charges, but EBS volumes and snapshots continue to incur storage charges.

consoleSteps.title: Create and verify the manual EBS snapshot
consoleSteps.instruction: In the EC2 left navigation pane, choose Volumes and select [VOLUME_ID].

instructions.text: In the EC2 left navigation pane, choose Volumes and select [VOLUME_ID].
Choose Actions, then choose Create snapshot.
For Description, enter fa-ec2-root-snap-001, then choose Create snapshot.
Choose the snapshot ID link in the success message and record it as [SNAPSHOT_ID].
Wait until Status displays Completed. Inspect Volume ID, Progress, and Start time.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The snapshot reaches Completed and identifies [VOLUME_ID] as its source volume.
consoleSteps.warning: Manual snapshots remain billable until deleted, even if the source volume is deleted.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 describe-instances --instance-ids [INSTANCE_ID] --query 'Reservations[0].Instances[0].{PublicIp:PublicIpAddress,PrivateIp:PrivateIpAddress,BlockDeviceMappings:BlockDeviceMappings}' --output json --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-ec2-learner
cliSteps.explanation: Run while the instance is running. Record PublicIp as [PUBLIC_IPV4_BEFORE_STOP] and BlockDeviceMappings[0].Ebs.VolumeId as [VOLUME_ID].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The JSON contains the current public and private IPv4 values and root volume ID.
cliSteps.warning: Record the public address before stopping the instance.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 stop-instances --instance-ids [INSTANCE_ID] --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-ec2-learner
cliSteps.explanation: Stop the EBS-backed lab instance.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response shows current state stopping.
cliSteps.warning: Wait until the state is stopped before the next command.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 start-instances --instance-ids [INSTANCE_ID] --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-ec2-learner
cliSteps.explanation: Restart the same instance after it reaches stopped state.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response shows current state pending.
cliSteps.warning: Wait for Running and use the new public IPv4 value when testing the page.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 create-snapshot --volume-id [VOLUME_ID] --description fa-ec2-root-snap-001 --tag-specifications 'ResourceType=snapshot,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-ec2-root-snap-001}]' --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-ec2-learner
cliSteps.explanation: Create a manual recovery snapshot and record SnapshotId as [SNAPSHOT_ID].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response contains SnapshotId in pending state.
cliSteps.warning: Manual snapshots incur storage charges until deleted.

verification.title: Verify persistent and ephemeral attributes
verification.instruction: Compare [PUBLIC_IPV4_BEFORE_STOP] with the running instance's current public IPv4 address, then inspect [SNAPSHOT_ID].
verification.expectedResult: The root volume and private IPv4 persist, the public IPv4 may change, and the snapshot is Completed for [VOLUME_ID].

tasks.title: Attach, resize, snapshot, restore, and reuse an EBS data volume
tasks.feature: Amazon EBS volumes, snapshots, and AMIs
tasks.goal: Create a gp3 data volume, mount it safely, resize it, restore it from a snapshot, and create an AMI from the configured instance.
tasks.whyItMatters: SAA-C03 tests EBS durability, Availability Zone scope, snapshot recovery, encryption, volume modification, and AMI-based repeatability.

consoleSteps.title: Create and attach the data volume
consoleSteps.instruction: Open EC2 in eu-west-2 and choose Volumes under Elastic Block Store.

instructions.text: Open EC2 in eu-west-2 and choose Volumes under Elastic Block Store.
Choose Create volume.
Select gp3, enter 2 GiB, and choose the same Availability Zone as fa-ec2-web-01.
Keep encryption enabled and add Name = fa-ec2-data-volume.
Create the volume and wait for Available.
Select fa-ec2-data-volume, choose Actions, then Attach volume.
Select fa-ec2-web-01 and keep the suggested Linux device name.
Choose Attach volume.
Connect through Session Manager.
Run lsblk to identify the new unmounted device.
Format only that new device as XFS, create /data, mount it, and write /data/lab-proof.txt.
Record the volume ID as [DATA_VOLUME_ID] and device as [DATA_DEVICE].

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The encrypted 2 GiB gp3 volume is In-use and /data/lab-proof.txt is readable.
consoleSteps.warning: Formatting erases a device. Confirm [DATA_DEVICE] is the new empty volume and never format the root volume.

consoleSteps.title: Resize, snapshot, and restore the data
consoleSteps.instruction: Select fa-ec2-data-volume and choose Actions, Modify volume.

instructions.text: Select fa-ec2-data-volume and choose Actions, Modify volume.
Change Size from 2 GiB to 3 GiB and confirm the modification.
Wait until the modification state is optimizing or completed.
Use Session Manager to grow the XFS filesystem and confirm /data reports the larger size.
Select the volume, choose Actions, then Create snapshot.
Enter fa-ec2-data-snapshot as the Name and create it.
Wait until the snapshot is Completed and record [DATA_SNAPSHOT_ID].
From the snapshot, choose Create volume.
Use gp3 and the same Availability Zone as fa-ec2-web-01.
Name it fa-ec2-restored-volume and create it.
Attach it to fa-ec2-web-01 as a different device.
Mount it read-only at /restore and verify lab-proof.txt exists.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The restored volume contains the original proof file and the source volume is 3 GiB.

consoleSteps.title: Create an AMI of the configured web instance
consoleSteps.instruction: Select fa-ec2-web-01 in Instances.

instructions.text: Select fa-ec2-web-01 in Instances.
Choose Actions, Image and templates, then Create image.
Enter fa-ec2-web-ami as the image name.
Keep reboot enabled so the filesystem is captured consistently.
Review the block-device mappings and create the image.
Open AMIs and wait until fa-ec2-web-ami is Available.
Record the AMI ID as [WEB_AMI_ID].
Open Snapshots and identify the AMI-owned snapshot as [AMI_SNAPSHOT_ID].

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The private AMI is Available and has a recorded backing snapshot.
consoleSteps.warning: The AMI and its snapshot continue to incur storage charges until deregistered and deleted.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 create-volume --availability-zone [INSTANCE_AZ] --size 2 --volume-type gp3 --encrypted --tag-specifications ResourceType=volume,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-ec2-data-volume}] --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-ec2-learner
cliSteps.explanation: Create the encrypted data volume in the instance Availability Zone.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 attach-volume --volume-id [DATA_VOLUME_ID] --instance-id [INSTANCE_ID] --device /dev/sdf --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-ec2-learner
cliSteps.explanation: Attach the data volume to the first instance.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 modify-volume --volume-id [DATA_VOLUME_ID] --size 3 --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-ec2-learner
cliSteps.explanation: Increase the EBS allocation to 3 GiB.
cliSteps.expectedResult: ModificationState becomes modifying, optimizing, or completed.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 create-snapshot --volume-id [DATA_VOLUME_ID] --description fa-ec2-data-snapshot --tag-specifications ResourceType=snapshot,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-ec2-data-snapshot}] --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-ec2-learner
cliSteps.explanation: Create the recoverable data snapshot.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 create-volume --snapshot-id [DATA_SNAPSHOT_ID] --availability-zone [INSTANCE_AZ] --volume-type gp3 --tag-specifications ResourceType=volume,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-ec2-restored-volume}] --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-ec2-learner
cliSteps.explanation: Restore a separate volume in the required Availability Zone.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 create-image --instance-id [INSTANCE_ID] --name fa-ec2-web-ami --description "Configured EC2 training web image" --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-ec2-learner
cliSteps.explanation: Create a private AMI with a consistent reboot.

verification.title: Verify independent EBS lifecycle
verification.instruction: Compare the source and restored volume IDs and read the restored proof file.
verification.expectedResult: The volumes are separate resources containing the same snapshot data.

verification.title: Verify the AMI
verification.instruction: Inspect fa-ec2-web-ami and its block-device mapping.
verification.expectedResult: The AMI is Available and its backing snapshot is recorded.

tasks.title: Build a two-AZ web tier behind an Application Load Balancer
tasks.feature: EC2, VPC, Application Load Balancer, and target groups
tasks.goal: Create a second public subnet and web instance in another Availability Zone, then distribute HTTP requests across healthy targets.
tasks.whyItMatters: Multi-AZ load balancing removes a single-instance failure point and demonstrates health-based routing at Layer 7.

consoleSteps.title: Add the second Availability Zone and ALB security boundary
consoleSteps.instruction: Open VPC and select fa-ec2-vpc.

instructions.text: Open VPC and select fa-ec2-vpc.
Choose Subnets, then Create subnet.
Select a different Availability Zone from fa-ec2-public-subnet.
Enter fa-ec2-public-subnet-b and IPv4 CIDR 10.0.2.0/24.
Create the subnet and enable auto-assign public IPv4 only for this training web tier.
Associate the subnet with fa-ec2-public-rt.
Create security group fa-ec2-alb-sg in fa-ec2-vpc.
Allow inbound HTTP port 80 from your recorded public IPv4 /32 only.
Edit fa-ec2-web-sg so inbound HTTP is allowed from fa-ec2-alb-sg rather than a public CIDR.
Confirm neither security group allows SSH port 22.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: Two public subnets exist in different Availability Zones and only the ALB accepts learner HTTP traffic.

consoleSteps.title: Launch the second web target
consoleSteps.instruction: Choose Launch instance in EC2.

instructions.text: Choose Launch instance in EC2.
Enter fa-ec2-web-02.
Select the same Amazon Linux 2023 architecture and instance type used by web-01.
Choose fa-ec2-vpc and fa-ec2-public-subnet-b.
Select fa-ec2-web-sg and fa-ec2-ssm-profile.
Expand Advanced details and paste the supplied web-b-user-data.sh.
Launch the instance and record [WEB_B_INSTANCE_ID].
Wait for Running and both status checks passed.

jsonBlocks.title: web-b-user-data.sh
jsonBlocks.content:
#!/bin/bash dnf install -y httpd systemctl enable --now httpd echo "

fa-ec2-web-02

Second Availability Zone

" > /var/www/html/index.html

consoleSteps.expectedResult: fa-ec2-web-02 runs in the second Availability Zone and serves its unique page.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not place both targets in the same Availability Zone.

consoleSteps.title: Create and test the Application Load Balancer
consoleSteps.instruction: Open Target groups and choose Create target group.

instructions.text: Open Target groups and choose Create target group.
Choose Instances, enter fa-ec2-web-targets, use HTTP port 80, and select fa-ec2-vpc.
Keep health check path / and create the target group.
Register fa-ec2-web-01 and fa-ec2-web-02 on port 80.
Open Load balancers and choose Create Application Load Balancer.
Enter fa-ec2-web-alb and choose Internet-facing, IPv4.
Select fa-ec2-vpc and both public subnets in different Availability Zones.
Select only fa-ec2-alb-sg.
Create an HTTP:80 listener forwarding to fa-ec2-web-targets.
Create the ALB and record [ALB_ARN], [ALB_DNS_NAME], [TARGET_GROUP_ARN], and [ALB_SG_ID].
Wait until both targets are Healthy.
Refresh http://[ALB_DNS_NAME] repeatedly and observe both server names.
Stop one target and verify the ALB serves only the remaining healthy target.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The ALB routes requests only to healthy targets across two Availability Zones.
consoleSteps.warning: ALB health checks fail if Apache is stopped, port 80 is blocked, or the target page does not return a successful status.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 create-subnet --vpc-id [VPC_ID] --cidr-block 10.0.2.0/24 --availability-zone [SECOND_AZ] --tag-specifications ResourceType=subnet,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-ec2-public-subnet-b}] --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-ec2-learner
cliSteps.explanation: Create the second-AZ public subnet.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 create-security-group --group-name fa-ec2-alb-sg --description "HTTP entry for training ALB" --vpc-id [VPC_ID] --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-ec2-learner
cliSteps.explanation: Create the ALB security group.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 run-instances --image-id resolve:ssm:/aws/service/ami-amazon-linux-latest/al2023-ami-kernel-default-x86_64 --instance-type t3.micro --subnet-id [SUBNET_B_ID] --security-group-ids [WEB_SG_ID] --iam-instance-profile Name=fa-ec2-ssm-profile --user-data file://web-b-user-data.sh --tag-specifications ResourceType=instance,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-ec2-web-02}] --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-ec2-learner
cliSteps.explanation: Launch the second configured web target.

cliSteps.command: aws elbv2 create-target-group --name fa-ec2-web-targets --protocol HTTP --port 80 --vpc-id [VPC_ID] --health-check-path / --target-type instance --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-ec2-learner
cliSteps.explanation: Create the HTTP target group.

cliSteps.command: aws elbv2 register-targets --target-group-arn [TARGET_GROUP_ARN] --targets Id=[INSTANCE_ID] Id=[WEB_B_INSTANCE_ID] --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-ec2-learner
cliSteps.explanation: Register both instances.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command returns without an error.

cliSteps.command: aws elbv2 create-load-balancer --name fa-ec2-web-alb --subnets [SUBNET_ID] [SUBNET_B_ID] --security-groups [ALB_SG_ID] --scheme internet-facing --type application --ip-address-type ipv4 --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-ec2-learner
cliSteps.explanation: Create the multi-AZ ALB.

cliSteps.command: aws elbv2 create-listener --load-balancer-arn [ALB_ARN] --protocol HTTP --port 80 --default-actions Type=forward,TargetGroupArn=[TARGET_GROUP_ARN] --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-ec2-learner
cliSteps.explanation: Create the listener forwarding to the target group.

verification.title: Verify Availability Zone diversity
verification.instruction: Compare both instance and subnet Availability Zones.
verification.expectedResult: The targets are in two different eu-west-2 Availability Zones.

verification.title: Verify health-based routing
verification.instruction: Stop one target and refresh the ALB DNS name.
verification.expectedResult: Traffic continues through the remaining healthy target.

tasks.title: Create a launch template and load-balanced Auto Scaling group
tasks.feature: EC2 launch templates and EC2 Auto Scaling
tasks.goal: Create repeatable web capacity across two Availability Zones and prove automatic instance replacement.
tasks.whyItMatters: Launch templates, Auto Scaling groups, load balancer health checks, and desired capacity form a standard resilient EC2 architecture.

consoleSteps.title: Create the launch template
consoleSteps.instruction: Open EC2 Launch templates and choose Create launch template.

instructions.text: Open EC2 Launch templates and choose Create launch template.
Enter fa-ec2-web-template and enable Auto Scaling guidance.
Select Amazon Linux 2023 and t3.micro.
Do not select a key pair because Session Manager is used.
Select fa-ec2-web-sg.
Set the root volume to encrypted gp3 with Delete on termination enabled.
Under Advanced details, select fa-ec2-ssm-profile.
Paste the supplied asg-web-user-data.sh into User data.
Create the launch template and record [LAUNCH_TEMPLATE_ID].

jsonBlocks.title: asg-web-user-data.sh
jsonBlocks.content:
#!/bin/bash dnf install -y httpd systemctl enable --now httpd TOKEN=$(curl -sS -X PUT -H "X-aws-ec2-metadata-token-ttl-seconds: 60" http://169.254.169.254/latest/api/token) INSTANCE_ID=$(curl -sS -H "X-aws-ec2-metadata-token: $TOKEN" http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/instance-id) echo "

Auto Scaling target: $INSTANCE_ID

" > /var/www/html/index.html

consoleSteps.expectedResult: fa-ec2-web-template version 1 contains the expected image, type, security group, role, storage, and user data.

consoleSteps.title: Create and test the Auto Scaling group
consoleSteps.instruction: Open Auto Scaling groups and choose Create Auto Scaling group.

instructions.text: Open Auto Scaling groups and choose Create Auto Scaling group.
Enter fa-ec2-web-asg and select fa-ec2-web-template version 1.
Select fa-ec2-vpc and both public subnets.
Attach to existing load balancer target group fa-ec2-web-targets.
Turn on Elastic Load Balancing health checks.
Set health check grace period to 180 seconds.
Set Desired capacity 2, Minimum 2, and Maximum 4.
Create the group and record [ASG_NAME].
Wait until two Auto Scaling instances are InService and healthy in the target group.
Terminate one Auto Scaling instance from EC2 without decrementing desired capacity.
Watch Activity history until a replacement launches and becomes healthy.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The group maintains two healthy instances and replaces the terminated target automatically.
consoleSteps.warning: The two original manually launched targets remain separate and are removed before the final scaling test if the learner wants only ASG targets.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 create-launch-template --launch-template-name fa-ec2-web-template --launch-template-data file://fa-ec2-launch-template.json --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-ec2-learner
cliSteps.explanation: Create the template from the supplied configuration.

cliSteps.command: aws autoscaling create-auto-scaling-group --auto-scaling-group-name fa-ec2-web-asg --launch-template LaunchTemplateId=[LAUNCH_TEMPLATE_ID],Version=1 --min-size 2 --max-size 4 --desired-capacity 2 --vpc-zone-identifier [SUBNET_ID],[SUBNET_B_ID] --target-group-arns [TARGET_GROUP_ARN] --health-check-type ELB --health-check-grace-period 180 --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-ec2-learner
cliSteps.explanation: Create the multi-AZ load-balanced group.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command returns without an error.

cliSteps.command: aws autoscaling describe-auto-scaling-groups --auto-scaling-group-names fa-ec2-web-asg --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-ec2-learner
cliSteps.explanation: Inspect desired capacity and instance lifecycle states.
cliSteps.expectedResult: DesiredCapacity is 2 and instances progress to InService.

cliSteps.command: aws autoscaling terminate-instance-in-auto-scaling-group --instance-id [ASG_TEST_INSTANCE_ID] --no-should-decrement-desired-capacity --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-ec2-learner
cliSteps.explanation: Simulate loss while keeping desired capacity unchanged.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response shows a scaling activity.

cliSteps.command: aws autoscaling describe-scaling-activities --auto-scaling-group-name fa-ec2-web-asg --max-items 10 --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-ec2-learner
cliSteps.explanation: Observe replacement activity.
cliSteps.expectedResult: A successful activity launches a replacement instance.

verification.title: Verify group boundaries
verification.instruction: Inspect minimum, desired, maximum, subnet, target group, and health check settings.
verification.expectedResult: The group uses 2/2/4, two subnets, the ALB target group, and ELB health checks.

verification.title: Verify self-healing
verification.instruction: Compare the terminated instance ID with current group members.
verification.expectedResult: A different replacement instance is InService and healthy.

tasks.title: Add CloudWatch monitoring, SNS alerts, and target tracking
tasks.feature: CloudWatch, SNS, and EC2 Auto Scaling policies
tasks.goal: Monitor EC2 and ALB health, receive an alarm notification, and let target tracking adjust group capacity safely.
tasks.whyItMatters: CloudWatch metrics and target tracking translate workload demand into automated capacity while alarms provide operational visibility.

consoleSteps.title: Create notification and health alarms
consoleSteps.instruction: Open SNS in eu-west-2 and create Standard topic fa-ec2-operations-topic.

instructions.text: Open SNS in eu-west-2 and create Standard topic fa-ec2-operations-topic.
Create an email subscription and confirm it from the mailbox.
Open CloudWatch Metrics and inspect AWS/EC2 CPUUtilization for the Auto Scaling instances.
Inspect AWS/ApplicationELB HealthyHostCount and UnHealthyHostCount for fa-ec2-web-targets.
Create alarm fa-ec2-unhealthy-targets.
Use UnHealthyHostCount >= 1 for one evaluation period.
Send the alarm notification to fa-ec2-operations-topic.
Record [SNS_TOPIC_ARN] and [UNHEALTHY_ALARM_NAME].

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The confirmed SNS subscription and CloudWatch unhealthy-target alarm are active.

consoleSteps.title: Create target tracking and observe controlled scaling
consoleSteps.instruction: Open fa-ec2-web-asg and choose Automatic scaling.

instructions.text: Open fa-ec2-web-asg and choose Automatic scaling.
Create a target tracking scaling policy named fa-ec2-cpu-target-tracking.
Choose Average CPU utilization and target value 50.
Keep instance warmup at 180 seconds.
Create the policy.
Review the CloudWatch alarms automatically managed by Auto Scaling.
Generate only a brief controlled CPU test through Systems Manager on one Auto Scaling instance.
Stop the load test after a few minutes.
Observe metrics and Activity history without waiting indefinitely for scale-out.
Confirm capacity never exceeds Maximum 4.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: Target tracking is active, metrics are visible, and any scaling remains within 2 to 4 instances.
consoleSteps.warning: A scaling event is not guaranteed during a short lab because metric publication and warmup take time; verifying the active policy and metrics is sufficient.

cliSteps.command: aws sns create-topic --name fa-ec2-operations-topic --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-ec2-learner
cliSteps.explanation: Create the operations topic.

cliSteps.command: aws sns subscribe --topic-arn [SNS_TOPIC_ARN] --protocol email --notification-endpoint [EMAIL_ADDRESS] --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-ec2-learner
cliSteps.explanation: Create the email subscription.

cliSteps.command: aws cloudwatch put-metric-alarm --alarm-name fa-ec2-unhealthy-targets --namespace AWS/ApplicationELB --metric-name UnHealthyHostCount --dimensions Name=TargetGroup,Value=[TARGET_GROUP_DIMENSION] Name=LoadBalancer,Value=[ALB_DIMENSION] --statistic Maximum --period 60 --evaluation-periods 1 --threshold 1 --comparison-operator GreaterThanOrEqualToThreshold --alarm-actions [SNS_TOPIC_ARN] --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-ec2-learner
cliSteps.explanation: Create the unhealthy-target alarm.

tasks.title: Operate and audit EC2 with Systems Manager, EventBridge, and CloudTrail
tasks.feature: Systems Manager, EventBridge, SNS, and CloudTrail
tasks.goal: Run a managed command without SSH, route EC2 state changes to SNS, and find the related EC2 API activity in CloudTrail.
tasks.whyItMatters: Managed operations, event-driven notification, and API auditing are distinct operational controls frequently compared in SAA-C03 scenarios.

consoleSteps.title: Run a managed inventory command without SSH
consoleSteps.instruction: Open Systems Manager in eu-west-2.

instructions.text: Open Systems Manager in eu-west-2.
Choose Fleet Manager and confirm the managed EC2 nodes are online.
Choose Run Command, then Run command.
Select AWS-RunShellScript.
Target one fa-ec2 Auto Scaling instance by instance ID.
Enter uname -a and systemctl is-active httpd as separate commands.
Run the command and wait for Success.
Open the command output and verify Linux details and active Apache.
Confirm no inbound SSH rule or key pair was required.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: Run Command succeeds through Systems Manager without opening port 22.

consoleSteps.title: Route state changes and audit API actions
consoleSteps.instruction: Open EventBridge in eu-west-2 and create rule fa-ec2-state-change.

instructions.text: Open EventBridge in eu-west-2 and create rule fa-ec2-state-change.
Use the default event bus and an AWS events event pattern.
Choose EC2 Instance State-change Notification.
Limit instance-id to the recorded fa-ec2-web-01 instance.
Choose fa-ec2-operations-topic as the target.
Create and enable the rule.
Stop and restart fa-ec2-web-01 once.
Confirm SNS receives state-change messages.
Open CloudTrail Event history.
Filter Event source to ec2.amazonaws.com.
Find StopInstances and StartInstances and inspect the acting identity, time, Region, and resource ID.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: EventBridge reports state transitions and CloudTrail identifies the API calls that caused them.
consoleSteps.warning: EventBridge reports service events; CloudTrail records API activity. They are complementary, not interchangeable.

consoleSteps.instruction: Match unpredictable short-term workloads to On-Demand Instances.

instructions.text: Match unpredictable short-term workloads to On-Demand Instances.

Match steady compute commitments to Savings Plans or Reserved Instances according to the required flexibility.

Explain why an Auto Scaling group provides replacement and horizontal scaling.
Compare EBS snapshots and AMIs for data recovery versus repeatable instance launch.
Compare public subnets with private instances using NAT or VPC endpoints in a production design.
Match cluster placement groups to low-latency tightly coupled workloads, not this web tier.
Match spread or partition strategies to appropriate failure-isolation requirements.

tasks.title: Delete every EC2 training resource safely
tasks.goal: Remove only the exact resources created by the EC2 Follow Along in dependency-safe order and verify that chargeable resources are gone.
tasks.whyItMatters: A complete teardown prevents unnecessary EC2, EBS, public IPv4, ALB, snapshot, log, and monitoring charges.

consoleSteps.title: Use the final reverse-order cleanup list
consoleSteps.instruction: Confirm the AWS account and eu-west-2 before deleting anything.

instructions.text: Confirm the AWS account and eu-west-2 before deleting anything.
Delete only resources with exact fa-ec2 names or recorded IDs.
Remove scaling policies and set the Auto Scaling group desired and minimum capacity to zero.
Delete the Auto Scaling group before deleting its launch template.
Delete the ALB before deleting its target group and security group.
Terminate the two manually launched instances and wait until Terminated.
Deregister the AMI before deleting its backing snapshot.
Detach and delete restored and source data volumes only after their instances are stopped or terminated.
Remove EventBridge targets before deleting its rule and SNS topic.
Delete VPC routes, associations, gateway, subnets, security groups, and VPC in dependency order.
Remove instance profile, role attachments, learner key, user, and policies last.
Verify every deletion before marking cleanup complete.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: All exact fa-ec2 resources are absent and unrelated AWS resources remain unchanged.
consoleSteps.warning: Deletion is permanent. Stop if a resource name or recorded ID does not match.
